text:
Devon P: tossing an idea out from the onprem upgrade playbook work: what if instead of big images we lean on a 'microbundle v1' protocol + operator handshake thats resumable and compact by default? low-bandwidth targets really need this.

Rina S: sounds promising. key asks? resume, verifiability, and simple rollback semantics?

Devon P: Exactly. sketch: split artifacts into small signed bundles (50-300KB). Publish an epoch manifest that references bundles by digest and gives an activation plan per component. Operator handshake consists of 3 phases: advertise -> stage -> commit.

Omar N: How does advertise work across airgapped media (usb / push servers)?

Devon P: Advertise is just a tiny signed index you can ferry over any medium. index example:

```
epoch: 2026-03-20T09:00:00Z
components:
  - name: modelserve
    bundles: [sha256:aa..., sha256:bb...]
    activation: [stage, commit]
signs: [sig-epoch-1]
```

Rina S: And stage means download+verify into staging area, commit does atomic switch?

Devon P: y

Jules T: Need determinism for out-of-order delivery. If bundle B arrives before A, node must be able to record partial state and not try to commit until all prereqs are ok.

Devon P: agreed. We store a per-component activation ledger (append-only journal) keyed by epoch+component. ledger entries are idempotent ops: staged(bundle), verified(bundle), committed(epoch,component), rollback(entry-id).

DeployBot: NOTICE: ledger entries should include monotonic 'apply-index' and signer metadata to avoid replay.

Omar N: UX: operator dashboards will drown if each bundle shows as its own object. How to surface useful info?

Rina S: collapse to component-level status in UI. UI shows 'component pending (3/12 bundles)', expand for details. Reconcile loop should debounce bundle events per component and surface errors as aggregated counts.

Jules T: Security: do we sign each microbundle or rely on epoch signature? Both have tradeoffs.

Devon P: propose hybrid: each bundle signed (enables independent medium transfer), epoch manifest also signed to provide intended activation order and expiry. Verifier checks bundle sig + that bundle digest is referenced by a valid epoch signature chain.

Omar N: Resume semantics? what happens on flaky 128kbps links?

Devon P: chunked transfer with checksummed ranges. operator keeps partial blob files and stores progress in the ledger. clients resume with a Range-like header. We also include an optional 'source-id' so same bundle from multiple sources merges into one staged blob.

Rina S: GC & compaction thoughts? nodes will accumulate lots of tiny staged blobs if left unchecked.

Devon P: TTL-based GC + refcounts from activation ledger. additionally a periodic 'compactor' can merge adjacent microbundles into a medium bundle when network permits; compaction produces a new signed artifact and an epoch bump. We provide `operator compact --max-ttl=72h` for manual runs.

Jules T: Rollback specifics: how to revert a partially-applied native driver vs stateless microservice?

Devon P: Activation has an explicit undo script per bundle when needed. For native drivers we require a 'safe-apply' hook: pre-check, dry-run, staged-undo. If component lacks safe-undo, operator refuses commit unless admin override. Documented in RFC.

Omar N: Observability: we need fine-grained failure types to avoid noisy paging.

Rina S: Agreed. events we emit: transfer.start/complete/partial, verify.ok/fail, stage.ok/fail, commit.ok/fail, rollback.ok/fail. Include component, bundle-digest, node-id, error-code. Wire to metrics + traces.

DeployBot: SUGGESTION: include a short integer failure taxonomy (1=network,2=auth,3=verify,4=apply) to make alert rules simple.

Jules T: Backwards compatibility: how do we upgrade old operator that expects monolithic images?

Devon P: compatibility shim: epoch manifest can include a 'legacy-image' pointer. When operator detects legacy mode it downloads consolidated medium bundle (server-side compaction) that packages microbundles into one. migration plan in RFC.

Omar N: Perf tradeoffs? signing each bundle increases metadata overhead.

Devon P: sign-size is small vs payload; we amortize verify by caching verified digests per-node and batching signature verification when importing an epoch (verify epoch sig then verify a batch of bundle sigs).

Rina S: Next steps: write a short RFC with sample ledger schema, operator API (advertise/stage/commit/compact/status), and a PoC that simulates 64-256kbps links + 5% packet loss.

Devon P: I'll drop a PoC branch and RFC draft by EOW. ping me if you want to join the PoC run. :rocket:
